name: Switzerland
summary: No tax on private capital gains from securities (federal law, all cantons), but dividends are taxed as ordinary income (up to about 39% in the City of Zurich, 22% in Zug, 43% in Geneva) and every canton levies an annual net wealth tax (top marginal 0.10%-0.86% depending on commune). Children are exempt from inheritance and gift tax in most cantons (not VD, NE, AI, partly LU and SO). National figures represent the City of Zurich; lump-sum taxation is available to non-Swiss newcomers without Swiss work in 21 cantons, not in Zurich.

regimes.name: Ordinary taxation (national figures = City of Zurich)
regimes.description: Ordinary residence taxation: federal income tax plus cantonal and communal income and wealth taxes. Switzerland has 26 cantonal tax systems; the national numbers here represent the City of Zurich (married couple, 3 children, no church membership). See data/subnational/CHE.json for all 26 cantons.
regimes.eligibility: Swiss tax residence: domicile with intent to stay, or a stay of 30 days with work / 90 days without work (DBG art. 3). Non-EU/EFTA nationals need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: No tax on capital gains from private movable assets (listed shares, bonds, funds, private company shares) for a private investor (DBG art. 16 para. 3; same in all cantons). Gains on Swiss real estate are taxed by the cantonal real estate gains tax; national figures represent the City of Zurich: up to 40% on gains above CHF 100,000, reduced 5-50% for holding periods of 5-20 years (about 31% after 10 years).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Private movable-asset gains are fully exempt; private losses are not deductible.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Applies only while the person is a private investor and not a professional securities dealer (ESTV Circular 36).
capital_gains.regional_differences: Securities exemption is federal and uniform. Real estate gains tax differs by canton: approximate effective rates for a CHF 1M gain held 10 years range from about 10% (GE, ZG) to about 40% (BS); Zurich about 31%. See data/subnational/CHE.json.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Gains can be recharacterised as taxable income: professional securities dealing; indirect partial liquidation (sale of >=20% stake to a company that distributes old reserves within 5 years, DBG art. 20a); transposition (sale of >=5% stake to a company you control at least 50%); liquidation surpluses and share buybacks are taxed as dividends.

open_questions: Real estate rate is an approximation for a CHF 1M gain held exactly 10 years on a non-owner-occupied property; actual tax depends on holding period, gain size and commune.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Securities: statutory exemption of private capital gains. Real estate: approximate effective cantonal/communal real estate gains tax on a CHF 1,000,000 gain, held 10 full years, not owner-occupied, computed from the ESTV Steuermäppchen 2025 tariff table. Foreign real estate gains are exempt in Switzerland.
capital_gains.professional_trader: ESTV Circular 36 safe harbour (all must be met): holding period of at least 6 months; annual transaction volume at most 5x the portfolio at the start of the year; gains not needed to replace missing income (gains under 50% of net income); investments not debt-financed, or taxable investment income exceeds interest paid; derivatives used only to hedge own positions. Outside the safe harbour a facts-and-circumstances test applies; if classified as a dealer, all gains become taxable income (plus social security contributions), but losses become deductible.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: No holding period for movable assets. For >=10% business holdings the partial taxation of gains needs 1 year (business assets only).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Gains on foreign securities and foreign real estate are exempt; foreign real estate counts only for rate progression in income/wealth tax.

dividends.summary: Dividends are ordinary income. Top combined marginal rate in the City of Zurich: 39.32% (federal 11.5% + cantonal/communal 27.82%, married tariff, church tax excluded). Only for holdings of at least 10% is the dividend partially taxed (federal 70%, cantonal 50%), giving about 22.0%. Portfolio dividends are taxed in full.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Partial taxation needs a stake of at least 10% of share capital: federal 70% taxable (DBG art. 20 para. 1bis), cantonal 50% taxable (StHG art. 7 para. 1, minimum 50%).
dividends.regional_differences: Top combined marginal rates on dividends in the cantonal capitals range from about 21.9% (Zug) and 19.3% (Wollerau, SZ) to about 43.2% (Geneva). National figures represent the City of Zurich.
dividends.important_exceptions: Church tax (if a member of a recognised church) adds roughly 1-3 points and is excluded here.

dividends.rate_basis: Marginal rate from the ESTV calculator (2026) on taxable income of CHF 5M for a married couple with 3 children in the City of Zurich, no church membership: (tax at 5.01M - tax at 5.00M)/10,000. Swiss 35% withholding tax is refunded to residents who declare the dividend.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Swiss companies withhold 35% Verrechnungssteuer on dividends; refundable to Swiss residents, reduced by treaty for non-residents (residual 0-20%).
dividends.treaty_network: About 100 income tax treaties (PwC: 99 in force at 1 December 2025). Non-recoverable treaty-rate foreign WHT is credited (flat-rate credit) against Swiss tax.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Company-level participation reduction for holdings of 10% or CHF 1M (DBG art. 69); see corporate. No structure is modelled: private capital gains are already tax-free for an individual, whereas a company pays about 19.5% (City of Zurich) on gains from stakes below 10%, and the participation reduction on dividends needs a stake of 10% or CHF 1 million, with 35% withholding and income tax on payouts.

wealth_tax.summary: Annual cantonal and communal net wealth tax on worldwide net assets (no federal wealth tax). In Zürich the top combined marginal rate is 0.642% (church tax excluded). Tax on CHF 10M taxable wealth: CHF 54,973; on CHF 50M: CHF 311,773 (0.62% average), before any burden cap.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: Social deductions for a married couple with 3 children: CHF 0 (the tax-free amount is built into the tariff instead). Household effects are exempt; debts are deductible. Listed securities are taxed at year-end market value (31 December).
wealth_tax.eligibility_conditions: Applies to all persons with unlimited tax liability in the canton (domicile or 30/90-day stay rules).
wealth_tax.regional_differences: Cantonal capitals range from 0.12% (Stans, NW) and 0.10% (Wollerau, SZ) to 0.86% (Geneva) top marginal rate. National figures represent the City of Zurich.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: No ESTV-listed burden cap for this canton.

components.name: Cantonal + communal net wealth tax (Zürich, 2026)
components.notes: Brackets are combined cantonal + communal marginal rates on TAXABLE wealth (after the social deductions in exempt_amount, here for a married couple with 3 children), derived from the ESTV tax calculator for tax year 2026 by evaluating the tax at each tariff breakpoint; the piecewise-linear schedule reproduces the official totals at the breakpoints. Church tax excluded. Foreign real estate and foreign permanent establishments are excluded from the base but count for the rate (progression). No general burden cap listed for this canton by ESTV.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Some cantons/communes levy a separate annual real-property tax (Liegenschaftssteuer) on gross real estate value; it is not part of the wealth tax.

inheritance.eligibility_conditions: Applies when the deceased/donor was domiciled in the canton (movable assets); Swiss real estate is taxed in the canton where it lies.
inheritance.regional_differences: No federal inheritance tax. 20 cantons fully exempt children (SZ and OW have no inheritance or gift tax at all). Exceptions: Vaud (up to ~7% in Lausanne above CHF 1M per child), Neuchâtel (3%), Lucerne communes (up to 2%, inheritance only), Solothurn (estate duty 0.8-1.2%), Appenzell Innerrhoden (1% above CHF 300,000). Geneva withdraws the exemption for heirs of lump-sum taxpayers.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Spouse also exempt. Other relatives and unrelated heirs are taxed. The JUSO popular initiative 'Für eine soziale Klimapolitik - steuerlich gerecht finanziert (Initiative für eine Zukunft)', which proposed a 50% federal inheritance and gift tax above CHF 50 million, was rejected on 30 November 2025 with 21.7% yes and by all 26 cantons (official result); there is no federal inheritance tax.
inheritance.foreign_assets: The canton of last domicile taxes worldwide movable assets; foreign real estate is not taxed. Switzerland has only a few inheritance tax treaties; gift tax is not covered by treaties.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Taxing right follows the last domicile of the deceased or the domicile of the donor. No tail after leaving Switzerland (except on Swiss real estate).
inheritance.summary: No federal inheritance or gift tax. Zurich (national standard) exempts children, grandchildren and the spouse from inheritance and gift tax for any amount. Most cantons do the same; see regional differences.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Full exemption for descendants, any amount.

regimes.name: Lump-sum taxation (Besteuerung nach dem Aufwand / forfait fiscal)
regimes.description: Income and wealth tax are replaced by a tax on a deemed income equal to worldwide living expenses, at least the highest of: a cantonal minimum (federal: CHF 435,000 in 2026), 7x annual rent or rental value of the home, and the control calculation (ordinary tax on Swiss-source income and assets plus foreign income for which treaty relief is claimed). The ordinary tariffs are applied to that base. Not available in Zurich, Schaffhausen, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Basel-Stadt; effectively not in Basel-Landschaft.
regimes.eligibility: Non-Swiss citizens taking up unlimited tax residence for the first time or after at least 10 years abroad, with no gainful activity in Switzerland (managing one's own private wealth is allowed). Both spouses must qualify (DBG art. 14; StHG art. 6). Non-EU/EFTA nationals also need a residence permit, usually under AIG art. 30 para. 1 let. b (important public, incl. fiscal, interests) or art. 28 (retirees), at the canton's discretion.

lump_sum.notes: National representative: Vaud (Lausanne), the canton with the most lump-sum taxpayers historically. Estimate for a family on an income base of CHF 1,000,000 (about 7x the rent of a CHF 12,000/month home): about CHF 459,211 a year (federal CHF 114,211 on CHF 1M at the ordinary tariff + cantonal/communal CHF 345,000 in Lausanne). At the cantonal minimum income base CHF 415,000 (federal minimum CHF 435,000 for 2026): about CHF 138,380. No separate wealth tax: the income base is increased by 15% (minimum 415,000 includes it; 7x rent +10%). Computed with the ESTV 2026 calculator (married couple, ordinary tariffs on the base). The real base is the higher of actual worldwide living costs, 7x annual rent/rental value, and the control calculation on Swiss-source income and treaty-relieved foreign income.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends are not taxed separately; they are covered by the lump sum unless treaty relief (reduced foreign WHT) is claimed, in which case they enter the control calculation (modified lump sum). Swiss dividends enter the control calculation at ordinary rates.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: No separate tax on foreign investment income within the lump sum.
dividends.regional_differences: Cantonal minimum bases and wealth surcharges differ.
dividends.important_exceptions: Claiming treaty-reduced WHT (e.g. on US, French, German, Italian, Belgian, Austrian, Canadian, Norwegian dividends under the respective treaties) requires including that income in the base and paying ordinary Swiss tax on it; otherwise the full foreign statutory WHT is suffered without credit.

open_questions: Which treaties require the modified lump sum to grant treaty rates was not re-verified for 2026 (ESTV Circular 44 lists them).
dividends.rate_basis: Marginal Swiss tax on additional foreign dividends is 0 once the lump sum is set above the control calculation; Swiss dividends taxed at the ordinary top rate (City of Zurich figure used as placeholder; Zurich itself has no lump sum).
dividends.withholding_outbound: Swiss companies withhold 35% Verrechnungssteuer on dividends; refundable to Swiss residents, reduced by treaty for non-residents (residual 0-20%).
dividends.treaty_network: About 100 income tax treaties (PwC: 99 in force at 1 December 2025). Non-recoverable treaty-rate foreign WHT is credited (flat-rate credit) against Swiss tax.

wealth_tax.summary: Actual wealth is not taxed: cantons tax a deemed wealth (typically 4x-20x the income base) or add a surcharge to the income base; this cost is included in the lump-sum estimate.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: Deemed wealth base set by cantonal law.
wealth_tax.regional_differences: LU, UR, SZ, NW, GL, ZG, SO, AI, SG, AG: at least 20x the income base; OW 10x; TI 5x; FR, VS, NE, JU 4x; VD +15% on the income base; GE +10%; BE only Bernese real estate; TG minimum total tax CHF 150,000.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Swiss real estate and Swiss-situs assets enter the control calculation.

regimes.duration_note: No time limit in law: lump-sum taxation continues for as long as the person keeps meeting the conditions of DBG art. 14 / StHG art. 6, i.e. remains a non-Swiss citizen with unlimited tax liability and takes up no gainful activity in Switzerland. It ends on naturalisation, on starting gainful work in Switzerland, or if the canton abolishes it (as Zurich, Schaffhausen, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Basel-Stadt did); the taxpayer may also switch to ordinary taxation. The tax base is reassessed annually and the cantonal minimums are indexed.

residency.tax_residency_test: Unlimited tax liability with Swiss domicile (residence with intent to stay permanently, centre of vital interests) or a stay of at least 30 days with gainful activity or 90 days without, ignoring short interruptions (DBG art. 3 para. 2-3). Residents are taxed on worldwide income and wealth, excluding foreign real estate and permanent establishments (exemption with progression). No exit tax on private assets on departure.

routes.name: EU/EFTA free movement (non-active persons)
routes.requirements: B permit (5 years, renewable) for EU/EFTA nationals without gainful activity who prove sufficient financial means and adequate health and accident insurance (AFMP; SEM).

routes.name: Non-EU: important public (fiscal) interest permit
routes.requirements: Discretionary cantonal residence permit under AIG art. 30 para. 1 let. b (important public interests), in practice granted to wealthy individuals who bring significant cantonal tax revenue, often combined with lump-sum taxation; cantons set their own expected tax amount. Subject to federal (SEM) approval.

routes.name: Non-EU retirees
routes.requirements: AIG art. 28: non-working foreigners above a minimum age set by the Federal Council (55), with special personal ties to Switzerland and sufficient financial means.

corporate.summary: Federal profit tax 8.5% on profit after tax (about 7.8% before tax) plus cantonal/communal tax. Effective combined rate on pre-tax profit for 2026 (ESTV calculator, CHF 1M profit): City of Zurich 19.5%, Geneva 14.7%, Zug 11.7%; PwC gives a range of 11.66%-20.54%. Participation reduction for holdings of at least 10% or CHF 1M market value (DBG art. 69-70). OECD Pillar Two: QDMTT from 2024, IIR from 2025, UTPR postponed (large groups only). Dividends paid out bear 35% Swiss WHT (refundable/treaty-reduced).
corporate.special_zones: No free zones. Patent box and R&D super-deduction exist at cantonal level (STAF 2020).

housekeeper_monthly.description: Statutory federal minimum gross wage for an unskilled housekeeper with 4+ years experience, CHF 22.30/h (NAV Hauswirtschaft art. 5, 2026) x 42 h/week x 52/12. A floor, not a market rate; employer social charges (~15%) and holiday pay supplements are extra. Cantons with their own standard contract (e.g. Geneva) set their own minimums.

cost_of_living.notes: Rent is a small listing-portal sample (15 October 2026). No reliably sourced figure found for family health insurance; omitted. Basic health insurance is mandatory and per person (cantonal premium regions).

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median monthly asking rent of the 8 distinct houses with 5.5+ rooms (about 4+ bedrooms) and at least 180 m² (one without stated area) listed for rent in the city of Zurich on ImmoStreet.ch on 15 October 2026; range CHF 4,000-9,800 (semi-detached and single-family houses in Witikon, Seefeld, Enge, Höngg). Very thin market: large family homes in Zurich are usually rented as apartments or on the Gold Coast (Küsnacht, Zollikon), where rents run higher. Asking rents as displayed.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain US-taxed. Swiss lump-sum taxation does not reduce US tax; to obtain US-Swiss treaty benefits on US-source income a modified lump sum (including that income) is generally needed. The Swiss private capital gains exemption does not shelter gains from US tax; Swiss income tax on dividends is creditable in the US.
open_questions: Imputed rental value (Eigenmietwert) abolition was approved on 28 September 2025 (57.7% yes); the Federal Council had not fixed the entry-into-force date on the EFD page checked. It will also abolish mortgage-interest deductions and allow cantons a tax on second homes.
Individual taxation (Individualbesteuerung) was approved on 8 March 2026 and enters into force by 1 January 2032 at the latest; married couples' tariffs used here will change then.

Cantonal tables used (partial taxation, burden caps, lump-sum minimums) are the ESTV Steuermäppchen for tax period 2025 (published 26 November 2025); 2026 changes in cantonal minimum lump-sum bases indexed to the federal CHF 435,000 were not checked individually.
Burden caps (BE, BS, VD, VS, GE, AG) can substantially lower the wealth tax for large low-yield portfolios and are not modelled in the brackets.
